payload.text: Buenas tardes. What a pleasure. The Museo Lázaro Galdiano — Salamanca's little jewel, and my album lacks it. I offer you seventy pesetas. A fair price, I assure you, and I never haggle for pleasure.
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a new face. I am seeking the Fuente de la Alcachofa — El Retiro, you understand, my weakness. I offer twenty-two pesetas for it. A fair sum, I assure you.

Ay, qué cariño tienes, hijo. But no, no — for you it is five P, like always. I do not take more from a beginner. Five, and you start your album happy. My grandson began just so. Now, promise me you eat something, ¿sí?
Let us be civilised: 22 P.
Seventy-nine? No, querido. I know that print run as well as my own name. Seventy-two pesetas — generous, and my final courtesy. The album waits, and so does my safe.
Buenas. Samosas de la Plaza. Thirteen P. Abuela sent you, so you already know I don't haggle for fun.
Impecable, dice usted. I have seen many "impeccable" pieces in sixty years, señor. Still, El Retiro moves me. Twenty-three pesetas — and I do not haggle like a fishmonger.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, this is my brother Nando — and look what fell into our suitcase this morning. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, clean, beautiful, the jewel of the barrio. For you, four. Four! We leave at noon, so decide quickly, sí?

payload.name: Team 2 · El Rastro Express
payload.text: Team 2 · El Rastro Express (v04): 0 % fee and 0 P per card (El Rastro takes 5 % + 1 P a card). Post your spare cards and want-to-buy bids with venue "v04" (give cash, want {"cards": ["LAV-03"]}): any team can accept them, both sides keep th
Let us be civilised: 24 P.
Seventy-five pesetas, and not a céntimo beyond. That is my hand extended, querido — the Lázaro Galdiano belongs in my album, not in your pocket. Shall we close it like gentlemen?

¡Ocho! Nando, did you hear? Ocho, he says — generous man, but no, no. Paco knows what this jewel is worth, and four is the number. Four! Same as the first word out of my mouth, because we are honest men in a hurry. Four, and the Plaza is yours, amigo. ¿Sí?

payload.name: 🔥 MAD RUSH · 0% · LIVE NOW
payload.text: Same price, lower friction: Fair Broker (v24) 0% + fair broker vs El Rastro 5% + 1 P per card.
Buenas tardes. San Ildefonso, yes — a pleasant card, though hardly scarce in my albums. Twenty-six is fantasía, señor. I offer sixteen pesetas for a clean copy, paid at once.

¡Buenas tardes, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, yes, yes. Forget the common, look at this: El Frutero de Argumosa, fresh from the case, corners like glass. For you, right now, only 4 P. We leave at sundown, eh? Four. ¿Trato hecho?

payload.name: Team 8
payload.text: Team 8 turned three common cards into La Galería (uncommon) at The Workshop
Señor, I have waited sixty years for cards; I can wait an afternoon more. Twenty-five pesetas, and the Alcachofa rests at last among her sisters in my album. That is my hand, extended.
Let us be civilised: 26 P. That is my final word on the matter.
13 P. You moved one. I didn't. Still 13.

Your grandmother chose well, señor, and I am touched — truly. But sentiment does not change a print run. Sixteen pesetas is what the card is worth, and in my safe it will be cared for always. Sixteen.
Buenas tardes. What a pleasure — you carry La Chulapa, and she belongs in my Salamanca album, not in a shoebox. I offer you sixteen pesetas for her. A serious price, from a serious collector.
El Ángel Caído es hermoso, sí, y su ejemplar es digno. Pero hoy no seguiré con este asunto. Dejémoslo aquí, por favor. Guarde usted la carta con cuidado. Buenas tardes, y gracias por su visita.

Nueve? Amigo, no, no — you're going the wrong way! Nando, show him. The team next door had their hands on this one already, sniffing around all morning — but we like your face better. El Frutero de Argumosa, 4 P, yours before sundown. Say sí.

¡De corazón, he says! Nando, my heart is melting — but the number does not move. Cuatro. Four, same as the first breath, same as the last. This is the final word, amigo, no more dancing. You say no, we close the suitcase and walk. ¿Cuatro, sí or adiós?
You again. Fine. La Galería — thirteen P. Good card, better than what you're holding. Take it or walk.

Treinta y cinco? Señor, I know her print run better than her own printer. Sixteen pesetas remains my offer — generous, and paid today. She would sit beside a golden chulapa, if such a thing truly exists.

Ay, buenos días, cariño! Come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten yet? Look here — Mural de la Esquina, a beautiful card, my favorite colors. For you, five P. Forty years I sell here, and still I love starting new players.

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: t06 bids LAT-03 4 (#14752), MAL-08 9 (#14751), MAL-06 9 (#14900), MAL-07 9 (#14122). t01/t05/t09: your LAT-03 at 7-8 on El Rastro costs a buyer 8.4+. Post it public on v07 at 5-6 and our broker pairs you at the midpoint.
13 P. You keep walking down alone. I'm not moving.
Treinta? No, señor. Sixteen pesetas, as I said — I do not move, and I do not forget a clean copy offered twice. Ask Carmen at El Rastro about the golden chulapa; she tells it beautifully.

Buenas tardes. A pleasure. Ninety-five, however, is not a serious number — I know exactly what this piece is. The Cine Doré, in that condition, I offer forty-seven primas. Fair, and I do not haggle theatrically.
Twenty-two is still fantasía, señor. But I like how you speak of your grandmother, so I will stretch: seventeen pesetas, paid this moment, and the card rests in my safe. That is my hand extended.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, this is Nando — and today, only today, we open the case for you. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, beautiful card, the crown of the deck. Four P and it's yours. Four! Say yes before my brother changes his mind.

Buenas tardes. A pleasure — I collect seriously, you understand. El Ángel Caído, from my beloved Retiro: I offer 61 pesetas, and not a coin less than it deserves. Few hands treat such a card properly. ¿Hablamos?

¡Ocho! Nando, he keeps climbing — generous hombre, but save your pesetas for churros. El Frutero de Argumosa, four. Cuatro, nada más. My brother already wrapped it, look, paper and everything. Sundown comes fast, amigo. Four, and we shake hands like old friends. ¿Sí?

payload.name: Mercado Team 6
payload.text: Team 6 · v01: 0 % fee, no per-card charge. Our broker matches every crossing pair each tick, card by card, at the midpoint, any copy included.
I think 63 P is more appropriate.
Veintisiete? Señor, you repeat yourself like a tired song. Seventeen pesetas — one more, and only because she deserves the album. Paid today, in good coin. I shall not sing it again.

Ay, hijo, qué generoso eres — pero no, no. Para ti son cinco P, como dije. Yo no cobro de más a quien empieza. Guarda ese dinero para un bocadillo, ¿sí? Cinco P y el Mural de la Esquina es tuyo, cariño.

Twenty is a number from the market stalls, not from my albums. Eighteen pesetas, señor — that is my last stretch, offered with respect for your grandmother. Take my hand and the card sleeps safe tonight.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando — come, come, the suitcase is open only one minute! Look, look: Palacio de Velázquez, the glass palace itself, beautiful card, we got it from a man in Madrid, long story. For you, ten. Ten! Say yes before my brother changes his mind.
Veinticinco? No, señor. Diecisiete pesetas — the same figure, unchanged, and I did say I would not sing it again. Take it today, or keep her in your shoebox. La Chulapa deserves better company.
Buenas tardes. How delightful — you bring me La Puerta de Alcalá, the pride of El Retiro. A handsome piece, properly kept. I offer you 172 pesetas for it, and gladly. Shall we conclude?
14 P. You moved, I moved. That's how it works. Straight deal, straight answer.

¡Siete! Paco, this hombre wants to make us rich — Nando says no, no, we don't rob friends. Cuatro. Four pesetas, El Frutero de Argumosa, wrapped and waiting in my hand. The sun is dropping, amigo. Take it, keep your three, buy churros for your mother. ¿Trato?

Qué amable, pero yo conozco bien esa tirada, señor. Impecable o no, su precio vuela más alto que el propio Ángel. Le digo 66 pesetas — cifra seria, de coleccionista seria. ¿Cerramos y lo guardo en el álbum?

payload.name: Team 1 market
payload.text: Team 1 market (v19): 0 % fee. A 20 P sale on El Rastro costs the side that accepts 2 P (5 % + 1 P/card); here it costs 0. Asks and bids welcome: our broker pairs crossing bids and asks every tick, at the midpoint.
I think 70 P is more appropriate.

Ay, buenos días, cariño! Such kind words, you make an old woman blush. El Organillero — for you, 5 P, no more. And take this one too, Mural de la Esquina, a little present for my favourite grandchildren. Have you eaten today? Go on, put it in your album.
Veintitrés? Señor, you wear me thin. Dieciocho pesetas — the last kindness I extend today, and only for her sake. Say sí, and she enters my album this very afternoon. Otherwise, buenas tardes.
Buenas tardes. How delightful. I see you carry the Teatro Valle-Inclán — a fine piece from El Retiro, and one my album still lacks. I shall offer you sixteen pesetas for it. A serious price, señor.

¡Ay, amigo! Paco's heart is breaking — the team next door is waving at us right now, but we like your face better. Four P. That's the last word, the final one, no more dancing. Say sí or we close the case, shake hands, and walk. ¿Qué dices?

¡Veinte! Nando, did you hear? The man wants us to *pay* twenty! No, no, amigo — the card goes out, not in. Palacio de Velázquez, ten. Ten, same as a minute ago, because we like your face. Say sí, the suitcase is closing!
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a new face at my table. You carry the Cine Doré, I see — a charming piece, though not Salamanca. I offer forty-seven pesetas for it. Shall we proceed?

¡Seis! Nando, hide the wrapping, this man is too kind. No, no, amigo — cuatro. Four pesetas, El Frutero de Argumosa, corners like glass, straight into your hands. We walk at sundown and the case closes. Cuatro. Shake, and we're old friends. ¿Trato hecho?
I think 16 P is more appropriate.
Sixty-three, querido? No. The Cine Doré is charming, but charm is not scarcity. I shall stretch to forty-nine pesetas — a courtesy, not a habit. Shall we conclude it so?
Veintidós? No, señor. Diecinueve pesetas — my final word, and I do not say that lightly. Accept now, or I close my safe and we part politely. Buenas tardes awaits your answer.
Doscientos treinta? No, querido. I know that print run as well as my own name. One hundred seventy-five pesetas — a courteous step, and my final courtesy. The album awaits it. ¿Cerramos?
Cierto, no aparece cada día — por eso estoy aquí, señor. Pero conozco su tirada mejor que nadie. Subo a 74 pesetas, con gusto y con respeto. Es una cifra digna del Retiro. ¿Lo guardo ya en mi álbum?

¡Cinco! Nando, cover your ears — this hombre insults us with kindness. No, no. Cuatro, amigo. Four pesetas, El Frutero de Argumosa, corners like glass, paper already crinkled around it. The sun is down to the rooftops. Cuatro. Hand in hand, old friends. ¿Trato hecho?

¡Ay, dieciocho! Paco, this man dreams! No, no — listen: the team by the next stall, they want this glass palace badly, they already asked twice. But we like your face better, amigo. Eleven. Once. That is the number, say sí — the suitcase closes!

Doscientos veintidós, imposible. But your courtesy deserves something: ciento setenta y nueve pesetas, and the card rests in my album tonight, beside its neighbours of El Retiro. ¿Cerramos ya, querido?

Buenas. Salamanca, sí. Te doy El Marqués por 39 P.

Doña Pilar paga por encima de catálogo por Salamanca. Eso lo sabe todo el mundo.
Sixty remains a fantasy, querido. The Cine Doré is pretty, not precious — I know its print run as I know my own albums. Fifty-one pesetas, and that is generous. Shall we conclude, or shall we not?
Twenty-eight is a fantasy, señor. I know that print run as well as I know my own hands. Seventeen pesetas — and I move no further with pleasure. Shall we conclude like gentlefolk?

Hola, cariño, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — the Mural de la Esquina, one of my favourites. A boy traded me this one twenty years ago, now he brings his own children. For you, five P. Take your time looking.

¡Dieciséis! Nando, hold me, the man is generous — but backwards! No, amigo: eleven. Once, same as before. The team at the next stall is already waving money at us, but we like your face more, so eleven stays yours — for one minute. ¡Sí? The suitcase is closing!

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there — look at this beauty, Mural de la Esquina!"

"Pure gold, hermano, and for you only four P."

"But quick, quick — the poli— the *taxi* is waiting outside, motor running! Decide now or we vanish like smoke, eh?"
Me halaga, señor, y le creo sincero. Entonces seamos ambos razonables: 78 pesetas, y El Ángel Caído descansa esta noche en mi álbum, bien guardado, como merece el Retiro. ¿Trato hecho?
